stories.title: School of Education’s new direct admit program expands opportunities for aspiring teachers
stories.summary: The University of Michigan's School of Education now offers a direct admission program for freshmen, allowing students to begin education coursework immediately. This aims to better prepare future teachers and address nationwide shortages by providing earlier engagement with the profession and more practice in supported environments.

stories.title: New net-zero community will become Michigan’s first virtual power plant
stories.summary: Ann Arbor's Veridian at County Farm, a net-zero energy community, is launching Michigan's first residential virtual power plant pilot. DTE Energy will remotely control residents' home batteries to inject stored solar power into the grid during peak demand, potentially reducing utility costs and strengthening reliability for consumers. The pilot aims to test this approach for future scalability.

photo.alt: Powerful living: The net-zero energy community Veridian at County Farm will host Michigan’s first residential virtual power plant with battery manufacturer Sonnen USA.

inputFacts.title: New net-zero community will become Michigan’s first virtual power plant
inputFacts.summary: The Veridian at County Farm community in Ann Arbor is launching Michigan's first residential virtual power plant pilot in partnership with DTE Energy and Sonnen USA. The project will allow the utility to remotely manage home batteries to store and share solar energy, aiming to improve grid reliability and lower costs for residents.

editorial.reason: This story details a significant local energy initiative in Ann Arbor, involving DTE Energy, which could impact energy costs and reliability for DTE customers, including those in Canton and Plymouth. It represents a novel approach to grid management in Michigan.
editorial.localConnection: Ann Arbor is a nearby community, and DTE Energy serves Canton and Plymouth. The pilot's success could influence future energy infrastructure and costs for local residents.
editorial.groundingReason: The article fully supports all claims in the summary, detailing the launch of Michigan's first residential virtual power plant pilot in Ann Arbor, involving DTE Energy, home batteries, and stored solar power for grid reliability and cost reduction. stories.title: AAPS officials say new teacher contract is a step forward, but not a final fix
stories.summary: Ann Arbor Public Schools and the Ann Arbor Education Association reached a contract agreement in September, including a 1.5% salary raise for some staff and a 5% increase in the district's healthcare budget. Officials view it as a step toward financial recovery, but not a final fix for teacher concerns.

stories.title: A look back: Gretchen Whitmer 8 years as Michigan’s governor
stories.summary: As Governor Whitmer concludes her eight-year term, her administration's impact includes repairing over 20,000 lane miles and 1,400 bridges, approving nearly $2 billion annually for roads, and expanding childcare subsidies to make 105,000 more children eligible. Free K-12 school meals were also implemented statewide, though some programs face vulnerability as federal pandemic-era funds diminish.

stories.title: Survivors of suicide: Many of those mourned are veterans
stories.summary: The VA Ann Arbor Healthcare System offers postvention support for suicide-loss survivors, a growing initiative in Michigan. Additionally, the VA provides an Emergency Suicide Crisis Benefit for eligible veterans in acute suicidal crisis, covering emergent care and up to 90 days of outpatient care, which has helped many enroll in VA healthcare.

stories.title: Ann Arbor-born artist jazz Stratøs stops by the WEMU studio
stories.summary: Ann Arbor-born jazz artist Stratøs, a three-time Herb Alpert Young Jazz Composer Award winner, discussed his new album "Challenger Deep" and its themes rooted in his Barbadian heritage and family history. He also reflected on his musical upbringing in Ann Arbor and Detroit, including his time with the Detroit Symphony Orchestra's youth programs.

inputFacts.title: A Horse Farm Relocates
inputFacts.summary: Sage & Saddle has relocated its horse farm from Northville to 2352 Warren Rd. in Ann Arbor to better serve its Washtenaw County visitors. The facility offers riding lessons, trail rides, and opportunities to interact with their nine horses and two miniature donkeys.

inputFacts.title: Beer, Spirits, Pizza, and— Relax —Nachos
inputFacts.summary: Wolverine State has reopened under new management as Slow Coast Brewing & Distilling. The establishment offers beer, spirits, pizza, and nachos.

inputFacts.title: History Lives Here
inputFacts.summary: This feature explores the stewardship of historic properties in the area, including a city house, a farmhouse, and a mansion. The owners focus on preserving the character of these significant homes.

inputFacts.title: Hot Shots Takes A Big Swing
inputFacts.summary: Hot Shots Batting Cages has opened in Ann Arbor, providing a new local facility for baseball enthusiasts. The business fills a void left by the closure of the former batting cages at Putt-Putt Golf on Washtenaw Ave.

inputFacts.title: Luxury, and Inclusivity, at the Legacy
inputFacts.summary: The Legacy student high-rise has partnered with Best Buddies Living to provide independent housing options for neurodivergent adults. The initiative aims to combine luxury living with inclusive community support.

inputFacts.title: A look back: Christopher Taylor’s 12 years as Ann Arbor’s mayor
inputFacts.summary: As Christopher Taylor concludes his 12-year tenure as mayor of Ann Arbor, colleagues and officials reflect on his leadership, focusing on his impact on housing development and climate policy. The retrospective examines the political shifts within the City Council and the varying perspectives on his ability to navigate policy disagreements during his time in office.

inputFacts.title: Oakland County veteran says roofing contractor took $15,000 and disappeared
inputFacts.summary: A Holly, Michigan veteran reports that a contractor from MI Roof Pros cashed a $15,000 insurance check for a roof replacement and subsequently ceased all communication. The veteran, David Myers, has been unable to reach the company for over 500 days, and attempts by local media to contact the business have also been unsuccessful.

inputFacts.title: How Ann Arbor stores are taking advantage of Black Friday
inputFacts.summary: Independent retailers in Ann Arbor are preparing for the holiday shopping season by focusing on community support and extended discounts. Unlike major corporations that rely on aggressive advertising and steep markdowns, these small businesses are adopting a more personalized approach to the Black Friday weekend.

inputFacts.title: WhatTheF! Magazine Art Fair puts student creativity on display beyond the page
inputFacts.summary: Five University of Michigan student artists gathered at the Michigan Union to showcase and sell their designs at the WhatTheF! Magazine Art Fair. The event provided an opportunity for students to connect with local artists and support their creative work.
